aluminium.ef_source: IFC India Construction Materials Database (2017) Table 14/Annex A, p.67 -- 'ingot', 31 kgCO2e/kg cradle-to-gate A1-A3, stakeholder-validated by Hindalco Industries, CEA-grid-adjusted (energy_derived_fraction_of_gwp 0.8968, from Table 16 Annex C p.75). See boq_carbon_extra_factors.json's original aluminium entry (kept on disk, deprecated) for the full sourcing writeup, including the by_product_form breakdown and the three corroborating India-specific sources -- that provenance detail was not lost, just not duplicated into every canonical entry here.
aluminium._reconciliation: boq_carbon previously used the raw, un-adjusted 31 kgCO2e/kg. wo_carbon's master file already had the CEA-adjusted 28.7632. Verified: apply_cea_adjustment_ifc(31, 0.8968) == 28.7632 exactly. Sourced+adjusted value wins.

blockwork_aac.ef_source: wo_carbon's master file carries TWO distinct, IFC-sourced block factors depending on block type -- AAC/aircrete block (this entry, 0.49284 kgCO2e/kg) and dense concrete block (blockwork_dense, 0.15946 kgCO2e/kg), a real ~3x difference. Kept as two separate canonical categories (not collapsed into one blended 'blockwork') precisely so wo_carbon's existing per-Activity-Code AAC-vs-dense distinction is preserved rather than lost in this migration.
blockwork_aac._reconciliation: boq_carbon's classifier does not yet distinguish AAC from dense block (one 'blockwork' regex bucket) -- its engine.py uses THIS entry (AAC) as its single default, since AAC is the more common modern specification in the two reference BOQs' block line items reviewed, replacing a rough unsourced placeholder (0.40 kgCO2e/kg). Splitting boq_carbon's classifier to detect AAC vs dense block (the 'aac'/'aircrete' keyword is already sitting right there in the existing regex) is a deferred, documented follow-up -- see the Workstream 01 reconciliation log.

plaster_cement.ef_source: IFC India Construction Materials Database (2017) Table 14 -- 'Cement based plaster', 0.4167 kgCO2e/kg. Kept separate from plaster_gypsum (not blended) precisely so wo_carbon's existing per-Activity-Code cement-vs-gypsum distinction is preserved rather than lost in this migration.
plaster_cement._reconciliation: boq_carbon's classifier does not yet distinguish cement-based from gypsum plaster (one 'plaster' regex bucket matching plaster/plastering/rendering/screed) -- its engine.py uses THIS entry (cement-based) as its single default, replacing a rough unsourced placeholder (0.20 kgCO2e/kg -- its own source note said 'consider replacing with IFC's direct cement-based-plaster line at 0.44, roughly 2x this placeholder'; 0.4167 is that exact substitution, CEA-adjustment not available for this line in either source file). This is roughly a 2x increase to every plaster line's GWP contribution on the boq_carbon side -- expected, and the single largest reconciliation delta of this workstream. Splitting boq_carbon's classifier to detect a 'gypsum' keyword (already proven real in Botanico BOQ text, see test_classifier_regression.py's gypsum-plaster test) is a deferred, documented follow-up -- see the Workstream 01 reconciliation log.

structural_steel._reconciliation: boq_carbon previously used 2.5 (the raw, un-CEA-adjusted IFC figure) via its own boq_carbon_extra_factors.json copy, which its own docstring flagged as 'not yet wired through ice_factors.py -- duplicated here for now'. wo_carbon's master_item_code_factors.json already had the correctly CEA-adjusted 2.34713. tile_ceramic.ef_source: IFC India Construction Materials Database (2017) Table 14 -- 'Glazed ceramic floor tiles', 0.62905 kgCO2e/kg (CEA-adjusted), wo_carbon's master file's own stated 'default'. Kept separate from tile_vitrified (not blended) so wo_carbon's existing per-Activity-Code distinction is preserved rather than lost in this migration -- though the two values are close (0.9% apart), so the practical stakes of this particular split are low.
tile_ceramic._reconciliation: boq_carbon's classifier does not yet distinguish tile finish types (one 'tile' regex bucket) -- its engine.py uses THIS entry (ceramic/glazed default) as its single default, replacing a rough unsourced placeholder (0.70 kgCO2e/kg) -- an 11% decrease. IMPORTANT SEPARATE ISSUE, not fixed by this value swap: boq_carbon's classifier's tile pattern also currently matches 'granite'/'marble' text, which should be priced as natural_stone instead (0.28514 kgCO2e/kg -- see that entry, ~2.2x lower than tile). That mis-bucketing is a materially larger error than the ceramic-vs-vitrified gap and is flagged as the higher-priority deferred classifier fix -- see the Workstream 01 reconciliation log.
